original_question: Suppose the edges of the hypercube Q_n are coloured red and blue. Determine whether there must exist a geodesic path between a pair of antipodal vertices that changes colour at most once.
target_in_paper: Section 8, Conjecture 8.1 of arXiv:2310.18163, which restates the Leader–Long geodesic one-switch conjecture; the closest fully formal original statement is Conjecture 4.4(B) in the cited paper "Long geodesics in subgraphs of the cube".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right combinatorial setting and conclusion: a red-blue edge-colouring of the hypercube Q_n, an existential statement about some antipodal pair of vertices, a geodesic path between them, and the requirement that the path change colour at most once. This is essentially the same problem as Conjecture 8.1 in the paper.
missing_details: The universal quantifiers should be explicit: the question is for every integer n (equivalently, for every n-dimensional hypercube Q_n) and every red-blue colouring of E(Q_n).
Q_n should be identified as the n-dimensional hypercube, with edge set E(Q_n).
The antipodal pair is existential and depends on the colouring; it is not a prescribed pair of opposite vertices.
Antipodal vertices should be defined as vertices that differ in all n coordinates.
A geodesic path in Q_n should be defined as a shortest path in Q_n, equivalently one in which no edge direction is repeated.
In this setting, a geodesic between antipodal vertices necessarily has length n; this is part of the nearby context and helps make the question stand-alone.
“Changes colour at most once” should be understood along the sequence of edges of the path, i.e. the edge-colour sequence has at most one switch.
Because the paper presents this as a conjecture/open problem, the research question should be phrased as a yes-no conjectural question rather than as a request to ‘determine’ it outright.
refined_question: For every integer n >= 1 and every red-blue edge-colouring c:E(Q_n)->{red,blue} of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, must there exist an antipodal pair of vertices x,x' in V(Q_n) such that x and x' are joined by a geodesic (that is, a shortest) path in Q_n—equivalently, a path of length n with no repeated edge direction—whose sequence of edge colours changes from one colour to the other at most once?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation (explicitly proved equivalent in Proposition 4.6 of the cited Leader–Long paper): for every antipodal red-blue colouring of E(Q_n), meaning c(e') != c(e) for each edge e and its antipodal edge e', there exists a monochromatic geodesic between some pair of antipodal vertices of Q_n.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's intended problem. In the collection paper, Section 8 states exactly this conjecture as Conjecture 8.1, with the same red/blue edge-colouring setup and the same conclusion about a geodesic between antipodal vertices with at most one colour-change. The immediately following context supplies the hidden definitions: the alternate antipodal-colouring formulation, the meaning of geodesic, and the fact that an antipodal geodesic has length n. To make the question fully stand-alone, those definitions and the universal quantifiers over n and the colouring should be made explicit. Since the collection paper is paraphrasing Leader and Long, the nearest fully formal source is their Conjecture 4.4(B), and Proposition 4.6 there explicitly proves the equivalence with the antipodal-colouring formulation. Theorem 1.2 and the resulting Corollary 4.3 provide the intended level of sharpness: the conjecture is not asking merely for a long monochromatic geodesic, but specifically for an antipodal geodesic with at most one switch.
